title: Hey!
subtitle: Hello, how are you, goodbye
review: Text by the author; notes and questions written by Claude: check them. No Burmese yet.
intro: A greeting meant for the cat, a car that will not run, a man who leaves for work three times and an urgent appointment in the bedroom: four short scenes between Emma and Lucas. Listen for how they say hello, ask how things are, and say goodbye.

lines.note: I'm home! = I am back at the house.
Honey: a loving name for a husband, wife or partner.

lines.text: Hello, my princess! How are we today?
lines.note: How are we today? A playful, formal way to say How are you?

lines.text: Oh! Very well, thank you. And you?
I was talking to the cat.

lines.note: What about me? = and me?
Hey is very informal. Lucas is polite to the cat, not to Emma.

lines.text: Hey. Your princess ate your dinner.

lines.note: How's it going? = How are you? Informal.
Good, good. A short answer is normal.
What's new? = Is there any news?

lines.text: Not much. Same old, same old.
lines.note: Same old, same old = nothing has changed.
Run: (of a car) to work. Running okay? = Is it working well?
More or less = not very well.

lines.text: What do you mean, more or less?
lines.note: What do you mean? asks for an explanation.
Won't run = does not work at all.
I'm doing fine = I am well.
I'm off = I'm leaving now.
See you tonight: see you + the time.

lines.text: Me again. Forgot my keys. See ya!
lines.note: See ya = see you. Very informal.
Catch you later = see you later. Informal.

lines.text: Okay, I'm really leaving this time. Bye!
lines.note: This time = now, not like the other times.
See you soon: you will meet again in a short time.
Slippers: soft shoes for the house.
Trash can (American) = bin (British).

lines.text: Oh, look at the time! Well, I'd better get going.
lines.note: Look at the time! = it is late. I'd better get going = I should leave now.

lines.text: I've just gotta go. See you later!
lines.note: Gotta = (have) got to. I've gotta go = I must go.

lines.text: No time. Gotta run! I'll call you!
lines.note: Gotta run! = I must hurry. I'll call you! = I will phone you.

lines.text: Then take the trash out on your way. Keep me posted.
lines.note: Take the trash out: carry it outside. Keep me posted = tell me what happens.

notes: Hey and Hi are informal. Hello is for everyone. Good morning and Good evening are more formal.
How's it going? and What's new? are friendly questions. Short answers are normal: Good. Not much.
See you + time says when you will meet again: See you tonight. See you soon. See you tomorrow.
See ya and Catch you later are very informal. Use them with friends.
Before you leave, say it first: I'm off. I'd better get going. Gotta run!
Gotta = (have) got to. Say it; do not write it in school work.

questions.q: You meet your teacher in the morning. What do you say?
questions.why: Good morning is polite. Hey is for friends.

questions.q: “What's new?” “Same old, same old.” What does the answer mean?
questions.why: Same old, same old = everything is the same as before.

questions.q: Emma asks about the car: “Running okay?” What does she want to know?
questions.why: A car runs when it works.

questions.q: Lucas says “I'd better get going.” What does he mean?
questions.why: I'd better get going = I should leave now.

questions.q: Your friend has an exam tomorrow. You want to hear the result. What do you say?
questions.why: Keep me posted = tell me what happens.
